prompt: Count the contiguous subarrays whose elements add up to exactly k. Values may be negative.
why: sum(i..j) = P[j] − P[i]. As you scan, count earlier prefixes equal to P[j] − k in a hashmap.
trap: Negatives break the sliding window: growing the window can shrink the sum.

prompt: An array is fixed, and you'll get up to 10⁴ queries, each asking for the sum between two indices. Make each query fast.
why: Precompute prefix sums once; each query is P[r+1] − P[l] in O(1).
trap: Many range questions over data that never changes means precompute.

prompt: In a binary array, find the longest contiguous subarray containing equal numbers of 0s and 1s.
why: Count 0 as −1. Equal counts = sum 0 = the same prefix sum seen twice. Store the first index of each prefix.
trap: “Longest contiguous” screams window, but balance isn't monotonic as you shrink, so a window can't decide when to move.

prompt: Return an array where each position holds the product of all other elements, without using division, in O(n).
why: Prefix products from the left × suffix products from the right.
trap: It's the multiplication cousin of prefix sums. The ban on division is the hint.

prompt: Decide whether an array has a contiguous subarray of length at least two whose sum is a multiple of k.
why: Two prefixes with the same remainder mod k enclose a subarray divisible by k. Hashmap remainder → first index.
trap: “Multiple of k” isn't monotonic either. Repeated remainders are the trick.

prompt: Find an index where the sum of everything to its left equals the sum of everything to its right.
tells: sum of everything to its left
why: Keep a running left sum; right = total − left − nums[i]. One pass.
trap: Squeezing two pointers in from the ends fails once values can be negative.

prompt: Given an unsorted list of numbers and a target, return the indices of two numbers that add up to the target in a single pass.
why: Hashmap of values seen so far: for each x, look up target − x.
trap: Two pointers needs sorting, which loses the original indices and isn't one pass.

prompt: Count the contiguous subarrays that contain exactly k odd numbers.
why: Prefix count of odds; for each position, count earlier prefixes equal to current − k.
trap: A window can do it as atMost(k) − atMost(k−1), but “count subarrays with exactly k” is the prefix-hashmap tell.
